name: Quantinuum
description: Quantinuum builds trapped-ion quantum computers and the software to program them, and sells access to them, mostly to governments, national labs and large companies. Its machines (H1 in 2020, H2 in 2023, Helios in 2025; Sol planned for 2027 and Apollo for 2029) are made in Colorado and installed in a small number of places, including one at Japan's RIKEN. Revenue is tiny and lumpy: $30.9 million in 2025 and $13.2 million in the first half of 2026, mostly cloud access, research and support contracts that are billed over time, against a $632 million operating loss in the first half of 2026 that includes large one-time stock compensation triggered by the IPO. Contracted backlog was $74.2 million at June 30, 2026, and a handful of customers, including the US government (about 30% of recent revenue), are most of revenue. Honeywell and other pre-IPO holders keep about 87% of the operating company's units through an Up-C structure.

hq.note: 303 S Technology Court, Broomfield, CO (June 5, 2026 prospectus); Quantinuum Inc. was incorporated in Delaware on January 20, 2026; the operating business also has UK roots (Cambridge Quantum)
